package_info.package_versions: unknown, but affected versions distributed in late March 2023
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp update was tampered with to include malware (TAXHAUL and COLDCAT), enabling remote code execution and targeted post-installation attacks on customer systems. The update chain was abused to deliver a malicious payload to downstream users, constituting a classic software supply chain attack.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious loader code that decrypts and loads shellcode (TAXHAUL), which in turn loads a downloader (COLDCAT).
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (likely, based on Windows binary analysis)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the code decrypts embedded shellcode and executes it in memory, which then downloads and executes additional payloads from attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate software updates should not decrypt and execute hidden shellcode or download further executables from the internet.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal update binaries only update application files; they do not contain hidden loaders or downloaders.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Self-updating mechanisms may download legitimate patches, but not hidden shellcode.
key_indicators: Presence of encrypted shellcode in update binary
Network communication to attacker infrastructure post-update

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Downloader shellcode (COLDCAT) that connects to C2 servers and fetches additional payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the shellcode establishes a connection to a remote command-and-control server, downloads further malicious payloads, and executes them on the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected outbound network connections to unknown infrastructure and execution of downloaded code is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not download and execute arbitrary code from the internet after installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may fetch signed updates, but not arbitrary shellcode.
key_indicators: Execution of code fetched at runtime
No user interaction required for payload execution

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises 3CX build/update process and injects malicious loader (TAXHAUL) into the 3CXDesktopApp update.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious update is distributed to customer systems.

attack_chain.action: On customer systems, the malicious loader decrypts and executes embedded shellcode.
attack_chain.leads_to: Shellcode (COLDCAT downloader) is executed in memory.

attack_chain.action: Shellcode establishes outbound connection to attacker C2 and downloads further payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-controlled code and potential further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from update binaries
file_indicators: 3CXDesktopApp update binaries with embedded encrypted shellcode
Presence of anomalous loader code in application executables
network_indicators: Connections to attacker-controlled C2 domains/IPs (as identified in threat intel feeds)
Unusual network activity immediately after software update
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor update binaries for embedded encrypted payloads or loader code. Detect post-installation network connections to suspicious domains. Use EDR/XDR to flag in-memory execution of code not present on disk. Correlate update events with subsequent anomalous process or network activity.
